findings.violation: The page title is empty, which makes it impossible for screen reader users to identify the page purpose from the browser tab or window title.
findings.fix: Add descriptive text to the title element, such as "Rider Service Updates" or similar page-identifying content.

findings.violation: The lang attribute value "translanguage" is not a valid language code according to BCP 47 standards, which could confuse assistive technologies about the page's language.
findings.fix: Replace "translanguage" with a valid language code such as "en" for English or the appropriate ISO 639-1 code for the intended language.

findings.location: Line 21, image element in s1 section
findings.violation: The image lacks an alt attribute, which means screen reader users cannot access a description of the image content.
findings.fix: Add an alt attribute with a descriptive text, such as alt="Platform update illustration" or a more specific description of the image content.

findings.location: Lines 16-24, heading hierarchy between h1 and h4
findings.evidence: h1 on line 16 "Rider service updates" and h4 on line 24 "Accessibility improvements"
findings.violation: The heading hierarchy skips from h1 directly to h4, violating the proper heading hierarchy structure which should be sequential (h1, h2, h3, etc.). This can confuse assistive technology users navigating the page structure.
findings.fix: Change the h4 on line 24 to an h2 to maintain proper sequential heading hierarchy.

findings.evidence: <div class="wizard-steps" id="s3-wizard"> with child divs having class="step"
findings.violation: The wizard component uses generic divs without ARIA attributes to indicate its purpose or current step state, making it inaccessible to screen reader users who cannot determine the component's purpose or which step is active.
findings.fix: Add appropriate ARIA attributes such as role="group", aria-label="Wizard steps" to the parent, and use aria-current or aria-selected to indicate the active step state.
